title: Vance Says US 'Investigating Very Fully' Kuhestak Wedding Strike as Death Toll Rises to 5, Voices Skepticism
detail: US Vice President JD Vance told reporters the US military is investigating the Sept 1 strike on a wedding gathering in Kuhestak 'very fully,' as Iran's reported death toll rose to five. Vance said 'the Iranian state media has not been a very good scribe about what's happened in the conflict thus far, so I'm extremely skeptical of this,' while insisting 'the United States never targets civilians in combat. We never will do that.' He also declined to call the six-month conflict a 'war.' Iran's Red Crescent has asked the ICC to investigate; Iran's UN envoy called the strike 'a grave violation' of international humanitarian law.

media.caption: VP JD Vance addresses reporters on the Kuhestak wedding strike investigation, Sept 3, 2026

title: Vance: US Won't Talk to Tehran Until Attacks on Gulf Shipping Stop; 40 Vessels Escorted Through Hormuz
detail: VP JD Vance said Washington is 'not willing to talk to Tehran' unless Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz cease, and that the US would use economic, military, diplomatic, and covert pressure to protect energy supplies and prevent Iran from rebuilding its nuclear program. He set no deadline for ending US operations, saying their duration depends on Iran's conduct in the strait. Separately, the US military said it escorted roughly 40 commercial vessels carrying about 18 million barrels of oil through Hormuz on Sept 2 as part of its protection operations. Brent crude ticked up 0.3% to $95.77/bbl and WTI rose 0.5% to $91.71/bbl on the news.

media.caption: VP JD Vance rules out Iran talks until Hormuz shipping attacks stop

title: Iran's Petroleum Minister Says Oil Exports Continued 'Even for One Hour' Despite Blockade
detail: Iran's Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad told ISNA that Iran's oil industry continues to find ways to circumvent the US naval blockade, saying crude sales and deliveries to international customers continued throughout the war — including during two separate blockade periods (April-June and since July 15) — by conducting sales and deliveries thousands of kilometers from the Persian Gulf and Sea of Oman. He said exports 'did not stop even for one hour' and described the situation as 'difficult but manageable.' Independent tanker-tracking data (Vortexa) shows Iranian port loadings fell to roughly 260,000 barrels/day in August — about 80% below the ~1.7M bpd loaded in August 2025 — suggesting exports have been sharply reduced even if not eliminated.

media.caption: Iran's Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad on oil exports under blockade, Sept 4, 2026

confidenceReason: Iran's official claim of uninterrupted exports contrasts with independent Vortexa tanker-tracking data showing an ~80% year-on-year decline in port loadings; both can be simultaneously true (exports continuing but sharply reduced in volume).
